Soojin / Marissa — posting preliminary feasibility notes from infra. Short version: platform can deliver multi-region failover today but the default configuration provides ~15 minute RTO and RPO on the order of seconds for model state (KV cache) if using async replication and cache warmup. To meet FinFabric's ask (RTO <= 5 min and RPO ~0):

Requirements / changes:
- Active-active deployment across US-West and US-East with synchronous state replication for critical KV caches (no async catch-up).
- Dedicated reserved capacity (hot spares) in each region to absorb traffic instantly; cannot rely on burst pools only.
- Continuous cross-region network health checks and automated session draining with pre-warmed caches (prefix caching + persistent snapshot streaming).
- Extended monitoring and dedicated on-call rota during initial weeks of live traffic.

Operational impacts / tradeoffs:
- Cost uplift estimated: 2.2–3.0x depending on model size and peak QPS (see attached calc).
- Slightly increased complexity in rollout; requires quarterly DR exercises and verification in production.
- RPO target: we can guarantee RPO <= 1s for user-visible data with synchronous replication; absolute 0ms (no possibility of any lost acknowledgement) is not a realistic promise given network-failure modes — legal will need to accept a small bounded RPO.

Attached: runbook_v2.md (draft), cost_uplift_calc.xlsx, high-level DR_design_diagram.pdf.

Laura Bennett
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
